solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Having restricted Southern girl, face sack

indicators.note: the face is said to hold in, or confine, the other pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: the face of a clock or watch is its dial
a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl from the south, now hemmed in, is about to lose her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having restricted' makes the face (of a clock) hold Southern girl inside it; 'face' and 'sack' both look like verbs in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissal is the act of firing someone, which is what giving them the sack means.

clue.text: She has medals mixed up

indicators.note: letters that are mixed up are jumbled into a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A woman owns a muddled collection of medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed up' rearranges MEDALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A damsel is an old word for a young woman, so 'she' can stand for one.

clue.text: Church council's case for Sunday: sign of agreement follows

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: a nod of the head signals agreement

explanation.surface: A church council argues for Sunday observance and others nod along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case for' means the outside letters of Sunday; the 's after council stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and church officials that governs church affairs.

clue.text: To be heard, I yell for cold sweet

indicators.note: something meant to be heard is spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: to yell is to scream, giving I SCREAM

explanation.surface: Someone shouts loudly to be noticed and ask for a chilly dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be heard' turns I SCREAM into its soundalike, the famous playground rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen dessert, a sweet in the British sense of a pudding served cold.

clue.text: Mag laden with scorn involved this guy?

indicators.note: letters that are involved are entangled and twisted together, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A magazine full of contempt has dragged in some fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges MAG LADEN and SCORN; the clue as a whole describes a gossip sheet's writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandalmonger is a person who spreads gossip and scandal, the guy behind a scornful rag.

clue.text: Absence of chess player, missing start

indicators.note: missing its start means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: in chess the two players are known as White and Black

explanation.surface: A chess player has failed to turn up for the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing start' drops the B of BLACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack is an absence or shortage of something.

clue.text: Margaret briefly referred to fixture for hanging

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the pet name loses its ending

parts.note: Peggy is a familiar form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret mentioned, in passing, a fitting for hanging things.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg is fixed to a wall or door to hang coats and hats on.

clue.text: Also in scheme — group of soldiers

indicators.note: the first piece goes in the second, placed within it

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
too means also

explanation.surface: A band of troops is included in the plan as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the word for 'also' inside the scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a military unit, a subdivision of a company of soldiers.

clue.text: Bet sporting contest's captivating Brazil's wingers

indicators.note: to captivate is to capture and hold, so the contest holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a game is a sporting contest

indicators.note: wingers play on the edges, so these are the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A wager on a football match that showcases Brazil's wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingers' gives B and L, the outer letters of Brazil; 'captivating' puts them inside GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: To gamble is to bet, staking money on an uncertain result.

clue.text: In Oman see where Minister lives

indicators.note: the answer is found in the clue words themselves, concealed in them

explanation.surface: A tourist in Oman is shown a government minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to the letters within 'Oman see'.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is a house provided for a minister, especially in Scottish Presbyterian churches.

clue.text: An assertion, outspoken, getting praise

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the words are taken by how they sound

parts.note: a claim is an assertion, giving A CLAIM

explanation.surface: A frank, bold statement wins compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' looks like 'frank' but signals that A CLAIM is said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic public approval, a synonym of praise.

clue.text: After restoration adore old place, fabulous

indicators.note: restoration rebuilds something, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Once it has been restored, I adore the old place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After restoration' rearranges ADORE OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado is the legendary city of gold, a place of fable sought by Spanish explorers.

clue.text: List flight manoeuvre

definitions.meaning: a ... is a list of names, as in a ... call
an aircraft's rotation about its long axis

explanation.definitionFit: Roll covers both an official register of names and an aerobatic rotation of an aircraft.

clue.text: One featured in theatre area for long period in the past

indicators.note: something featured in another appears inside it

parts.note: the stage is the performing area of a theatre

explanation.surface: Someone who appeared on a theatre's stage for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' puts One within the theatre area, read as a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric era when tools were made of stone, lasting millions of years.

clue.text: Almost all of plan referring to births rejected as a sham

indicators.note: almost all means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: natal means relating to birth

explanation.surface: Nearly the whole of a maternity plan is thrown out as fraudulent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost all of' trims CHART to CHAR; 'rejected' turns NATAL into LATAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham can be a person who is a fraud or impostor, which a charlatan is.

clue.text: Partner's argument against — so right!

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A partner objects to something, then exclaims that it is so true.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse or companion, especially of a monarch.

clue.text: Upcoming student's mistake

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pupil is a student, so student's gives PUPIL'S

explanation.surface: A student is about to make an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' reads PUPILS upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a careless error or blunder.

clue.text: One observing son at door maybe?

parts.note: a door is one example of an entry

explanation.surface: Perhaps a son stands at the door keeping watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a guard posted to watch for danger.

clue.text: Connect learner with writing material

parts.note: L stands for learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car
ink is a material used for writing

explanation.surface: Pair a pupil with pens and ink.
explanation.definitionFit: To link is to join or connect things together.

clue.text: Hope to include sailors, very good apparently, in lively dance

indicators.note: one word includes the others, holding them inside it

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors
pi is slang for pious, so it means very good, apparently virtuous

explanation.surface: Someone hopes the seemingly well-behaved sailors join a spirited dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts sailors and 'very good' inside Hope; PI is short for pious, hence 'apparently' good.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is a vigorous solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: At the outset innovative agreement is perfect

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: An agreement that is innovative from the start is flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the outset' gives the I of innovative.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, matching the best imaginable standard.

clue.text: Imported by Mykonos, healthy food

indicators.note: imported means carried in, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Healthy food has been brought in to the Greek island of Mykonos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imported by' points to the letters within 'Mykonos, healthy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food.

clue.text: Extend short programme covering half of our capital

indicators.note: one piece covers the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: prog is a short form of programme

indicators.note: half of means only the first three of the six letters are kept

parts.note: for a British paper, our capital is London

explanation.surface: A brief programme about part of London is stretched out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our capital' is London because this is a British paper; 'half of' keeps its first three letters, and 'covering' wraps the short programme round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong something is to make it last longer, to extend it.

clue.text: Watchful as lazy employee reads tabloid at first

indicators.note: at first means each of these words gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Keep an eye out while an idle worker browses a tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the first letters of 'as lazy employee reads tabloid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alert means watchful and ready to notice danger.

clue.text: Bringing back best trophy

indicators.note: bringing back means the word is returned, read backwards

parts.note: top means best

explanation.surface: Bringing home the top trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing back' turns TOP around.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is slang for a cup or trophy won in sport.

clue.text: Knockabout fun as her ploy goes wrong

indicators.note: a plan that goes wrong falls apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Her scheme collapses into slapstick fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' rearranges AS + HER PLOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Horseplay is rough, boisterous play, the knockabout kind.
